title: The Rhythm of the Lord's Day: How a Mother and Wife Can Help Her Family Make the Most of Sundays
author: Foster, Michael
summary: The Lord's Day (Sunday) provides a rhythm and structure to family life that modern culture has largely abandoned. Foster argues that mothers and wives can reinstitute this rhythm by honoring Sunday differently—setting aside work, media, and busyness in favor of rest, worship, family, and intentional presence. This is not legalism but wisdom: families that honor a sacred day report greater cohesion, better relationships, and children who develop healthy rhythms of work and rest. The family that gathers on Sunday—for worship, for a meal, for presence—is investing in deep relational bonds. Women who set the tone for household rhythms have enormous power to restore sacred time to family life.
points: A sacred day (Sunday) provides rhythm and structure that strengthens family bonds.
Mothers who set the tone for household can restore sacred time to family life.
Families that honor a set-apart day report greater cohesion and deeper relationships.
Rest and intentional presence on Sunday create the conditions for real family connection.
quotes: The Lord's Day is not a constraint on family life but the framework that makes it rich.
Mothers have the power to restore sacred time to the home by how they honor one day each week.
A family that gathers for worship and presence on Sunday is investing in bonds that last.” Archived from We Made People Substack on May 2, 2026 by Tim.
